slides.0.title: Hunter Valley: The Miracle of Sémillon
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 4 · Lesson 3
slides.1.title: Hunter Valley: Background
slides.1.points.0: Location: 160 km north of Sydney; Australia's oldest wine region (since 1820s)
slides.1.points.1: Climate: subtropical with high humidity and unpredictable rain — challenging viticulture
slides.1.points.2: Soil: alluvial red clay loam and sandy loam in the Lower Hunter
slides.1.points.3: Two sub-regions: Lower Hunter (traditional, near Cessnock) and Upper Hunter (warmer, more irrigated)
slides.1.points.4: Key varieties: Sémillon (white) + Shiraz (red) — both in world-class expressions
slides.2.title: Hunter Sémillon: The 20-Year Transformation
slides.2.points.0: Harvested very early (January) — when grapes barely reach 10–11% potential alcohol
slides.2.points.1: Young (0–3 years): almost neutral — lemon zest, lanolin, slight grassiness
slides.2.points.2: Mid (5–8 years): starting to show toast, hay, waxy lemon
slides.2.points.3: Mature (10–15 years): full honey, buttered toast, beeswax, lanolin — no oak needed
slides.2.points.4: Peak (15–20+ years): extraordinary complexity, still vibrant acidity — great Sémillon outlives many red wines
slides.3.title: Hunter Valley Shiraz
slides.3.points.0: Style: medium-bodied, savoury, earthy — 'sweaty saddle' and leather complexity
slides.3.points.1: Not the concentrated Barossa style — Hunter Shiraz is about finesse and regional character
slides.3.points.2: Also ages wonderfully; develops secondary complexity with 10+ years
slides.3.points.3: Top producers: Tyrrell's (Vat 1 Sémillon iconic), McWilliam's, Brokenwood, Lindeman's
slides.4.question: Hunter Valley Sémillon is picked at very low sugar ripeness (10–11% alcohol). Why does this make it special?
slides.4.options.0: It makes the wine cheaper to produce
slides.4.options.1: Early picking preserves extreme acidity, which protects the wine for 20+ years of bottle evolution — developing honey, toast and beeswax without any oak
slides.4.options.2: Low alcohol means the wine can be sold as 'diet wine'
slides.4.options.3: Early picking prevents the grapes from rotting in the humid climate
slides.4.explanation: Hunter Valley Sémillon is deliberately harvested early when sugar levels are minimal, creating naturally low alcohol and sky-high acidity. This acidity acts as a natural preservative, allowing the wine to evolve in bottle for 15–20+ years without any oak support. The result — honey, toast and beeswax from a humble white grape — is one of the world's most astonishing ageing wines.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Hunter Valley: oldest NSW wine region; subtropical climate; renowned for unique whites
slides.5.points.1: Sémillon: 10–11% abv, no oak, extreme acidity → transforms into honey+toast complexity over 15–20 years
slides.5.points.2: Hunter Shiraz: savoury, medium-bodied, earthy — finesse over power; Tyrrell's Vat 9 is benchmark
